record_type_quote: The current study attempted to equate the sadness intensities between the interpersonal and non-interpersonal mood inductions. After equating the intensity of the sadness (interpersonal vs. non-interpersonal), the present studies failed to replicate Lee et al.’s findings (2013, study 3) in that they found no differences in music preferences between the interpersonal versus non-interpersonal sadness groups when they were of equal intensity.

targets.outcome_quote: After equating the intensity of the sadness (interpersonal vs. non-interpersonal), the present studies failed to replicate Lee et al.’s findings (2013, study 3) in that they found no differences in music preferences between the interpersonal versus non-interpersonal sadness groups when they were of equal intensity. However, consistent with Lee et al.’s findings, people in the interpersonal sadness group did show stronger mood-congruent preferences than those in the neutral group in both studies.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The abstract explicitly contrasts failure of the interpersonal versus non-interpersonal comparison with successful interpersonal versus neutral comparisons in both studies. The failed wording is qualified to one comparison, rather than an overall verdict.
